prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: low-speed head-on collision in League City, Texas. Injury: whiplash. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1016; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my full name on the record, but I can confirm I'm the plaintiff in this matter.

Q: Fair enough. Let's talk about the collision. Where were you when it happened?
A: I was driving on a two-lane road in League City, Texas, heading toward a grocery store. It was a weekday afternoon and traffic was light.

Q: What were you doing right before impact?
A: I had slowed down for a turn signal ahead. The other car came across the center line. I braked as hard as I could, but we still collided head-on.

Q: How fast would you estimate you were going?
A: Not fast. Maybe twenty or twenty-five miles an hour. It didn't feel like a high-speed crash. The airbags did not deploy.

Q: Did you lose consciousness or hit your head?
A: No. I didn't hit my head. I was jolted forward and then pushed back into the seat. My neck snapped, and I felt it right away.

Q: When did the neck pain begin?
A: Within a few hours, it was stiff and sore. By the next morning, the pain had spread into my shoulders and I had headaches at the base of my skull.

Q: Did you seek medical care?
A: Yes. I went to an urgent care clinic that same evening, and then I started physical therapy about a week later. I've been going about two or three times a week since.

Q: Are you still receiving treatment?
A: Yes. My doctor has me doing exercises at home, and I still use a heating pad most nights.

Q: How has this affected your daily routine?
A: I have trouble sleeping through the night because I can't find a comfortable position. I've had to cut back on yard work and I stopped going to my weekend pickleball league for now. Lifting groceries out of the trunk hurts.

Q: Has anyone else been able to help with those tasks?
A: My spouse has taken on more of the cooking and cleaning. I'm trying to push through it, but some days are harder than others.
